tagline: Harbour commuter spine meets the Cape & Islands.
summary: Boston pairs a dense inner-harbour commuter network — MBTA and private ferries from Long Wharf and Rowes Wharf to Hingham, Hull and the Harbor Islands — with one of the world's great seasonal island markets in Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard, where Steamship Authority diesel ferries carried roughly 2.9 million passengers in 2022 and routinely hit summer capacity limits. All of it now sits under a state net-zero-by-2050 climate mandate and a fast-growing offshore-wind sector that are driving demand for cleaner vessels.

journeys.with_navier: A direct foiling run across Cape Cod Bay

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Harbour commutes (~9 nm) and marquee island crossings (Hyannis↔Nantucket ~26 nm, Boston↔Provincetown ~42 nm, Boston↔Newport ~58 nm) all sit inside the all-electric envelope.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Reserved for the longest combined corridors and outer-island chaining where all-weather range matters.

competitive_landscape: Today: MBTA and private harbour ferries plus the seasonal Steamship Authority and Hy-Line diesel fleets to the islands. The pain is summer capacity crunch and weather exposure — the status quo a faster, cleaner tier improves on.
seasonality: Strong summer island season; winter focused on the harbour commuter network. Open crossings handled by routing and the hybrid.
regulatory_note: Massachusetts has binding climate targets and a growing offshore-wind sector driving demand for cleaner vessels; harbour commuter ferries are publicly contracted — a procurement pathway.

precedents.what: A foiling-electric vessel network at national scale (~100 vessels / $100M, 3-year phasing)
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves foiling-electric works as an at-scale transfer-and-island-hopping network, not just a pilot.
